## 1. Purpose

This SOP describes procedures for characterizing the physical habitat
of wadeable streams using the quantitative transect-based protocol
developed by the California State Water Resources Control Board's
Surface Water Ambient Monitoring Program (SWAMP). Physical habitat
data document the structural condition of streams -- channel
dimensions, substrate composition, bank stability, riparian
vegetation, instream cover, and human influence -- and are essential
for interpreting bioassessment results and diagnosing the causes of
biological impairment.

The protocol produces data compatible with the California Index of
Physical-habitat Integrity (IPI), the California Stream Condition
Index (CSCI), and the Algal Stream Condition Index (ASCI), enabling
direct comparison with statewide reference data maintained by SWAMP
and the Southern California Coastal Water Research Project (SCCWRP).


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Wadeable perennial and intermittent streams and
  rivers where personnel can safely wade to make measurements
  (generally depths less than approximately 1 m and velocities less
  than approximately 1.2 m/s at the time of sampling)
- **Does not apply to:** Non-wadeable rivers requiring boat-based
  protocols; estuarine or tidal reaches; depressional wetlands (use
  CRAM instead); lake or reservoir shorelines
- **Location:** All EA Program stream monitoring sites, including
  tributaries to the Santa Ana River watershed and other southern
  California waterbodies


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Project Lead | Approve site selection and sampling design              |
| Field Lead        | Coordinate logistics, lead reach delineation, verify equipment |
| Trained Personnel | Collect physical habitat data per this SOP              |
| New Students      | Complete training before participating in field crews   |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Drowning and swift water:** Do not wade in flows deeper than
  approximately waist height or where footing is unstable. Always face
  upstream. Use a wading rod for support.
- **Slippery substrates:** Algae-covered cobble and bedrock are
  extremely slippery. Wear felt-soled or studded wading boots.
- **Biological:** Waterborne pathogens, poison oak along riparian
  corridors, ticks, snakes, and stinging insects. Check for ticks
  after every field day.
- **Heat:** Southern California field sites can exceed 40 C during
  summer. Carry adequate water and take shade breaks.
- **Sensitive species:** California red-legged frog, arroyo toad,
  least Bell's vireo, southwestern willow flycatcher, and steelhead
  may be present at some sites. Consult permit requirements before
  sampling (Section 4.2).
:::

### 4.1 Required PPE

- [ ] Chest or hip waders (neoprene or breathable)
- [ ] Wading boots with felt or studded soles
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen, long sleeves)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (when handling samples or in contact with
      potentially contaminated water)

### 4.2 Permits

Sampling in or near habitat for listed species may require a
Scientific Collecting Permit (CDFW) and/or a Section 10/Section 7
consultation (USFWS). The PI must confirm permit status before
fieldwork at any new site. At some sites, a permitted biologist
escort may be required.

### 4.3 Invasive Species Prevention

Decontaminate all equipment (waders, nets, measuring tapes, wading
rods) between sites to prevent transfer of invasive species and
pathogens (e.g., *Didymosphenia geminata*, New Zealand mudsnails).
Inspect, scrub, and dry all gear, or treat with a dilute bleach
solution or 60 C hot water.

### 4.4 Emergency Procedures

A minimum of two people must be present for any in-stream work. If a
team member loses footing, release equipment and float feet-first
downstream to a recovery point. Refer to
[SOP-F01 Field Safety](SOP-F01-field-safety.qmd) for general
emergency procedures.

## 6. Estimated Time

| Task                                  | Time (2-person crew)                     |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Reach delineation and transect setup  | 20--30 minutes                           |
| Full physical habitat assessment (Modules C--M) | 1.5--2.5 hours                |
| Slope and sinuosity (Module L)        | 20--40 minutes                           |
| Photographs (Module M)               | 10--15 minutes                           |
| Total                                 | 2--3.5 hours per reach                   |


## 7. Procedure

### 7.1 Reach Delineation

The sampling reach defines the stream segment over which all
measurements are collected. Reach length depends on stream size:

| Average Wetted Width | Reach Length | Number of Main Transects |
|:---------------------|:-------------|:-------------------------|
| 10 m or less         | 150 m        | 11 (A--K)                |
| Greater than 10 m    | 250 m        | 11 (A--K)                |

1. Identify the downstream boundary of the reach. This is Transect A
   (station 0 m).
2. Measure upstream to establish the reach length (150 m or 250 m).
   The upstream boundary is Transect K.
3. Space the 11 main transects (A through K) equally along the reach.
   For a 150 m reach, transects are 15 m apart; for a 250 m reach,
   they are 25 m apart.
4. Mark 10 inter-transects (AB, BC, CD, ... JK) at the midpoint
   between each pair of main transects.
5. Flag each transect with flagging tape on both banks.
6. Record GPS coordinates at Transect A and Transect K.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Working Direction
Always work in an upstream direction (A to K) to minimize disturbance
of the substrate and water column at transects you have not yet
measured.
:::

### 7.2 Notable Field Conditions

Before beginning measurements, record the following on the field
form:

- Date, time, crew members
- Recent precipitation (last 48 hours)
- Evidence of recent scour (displaced cobble, fresh sediment deposits,
  debris lines, lack of periphyton on substrates)
- Whether the reach lies within an engineered channel (concrete-lined,
  rip-rap, gabions)
- General flow conditions (baseflow, elevated, or declining)

If recent scour is suspected, mark "Yes" on the field form so the
data can be flagged in the database.


### 7.3 Module C: Wetted Width and Bankfull Dimensions

At each main transect (A--K) and each inter-transect (AB--JK):

1. Stretch the measuring tape perpendicular to flow across the
   wetted channel
2. Measure and record **wetted width** to the nearest 0.1 m (for
   widths up to 3 m) or to the nearest 5% of the width (for
   widths greater than 3 m)
3. At main transects only, also measure **bankfull width** and
   **bankfull height** (the vertical distance from the water
   surface to the bankfull stage indicator)
4. Bankfull indicators include the top of point bars, changes in
   vegetation from aquatic to terrestrial, changes in bank slope,
   stain lines, and the lower boundary of lichens on rocks

### 7.4 Module D: Substrate Size, Depth, and CPOM

At each transect (main and inter), measure substrate at five equally
spaced points across the wetted channel (at the 1/5, 2/5, thalweg,
3/5, and 4/5 positions from right bank to left bank):

1. At each point, measure **water depth** to the nearest cm using
   the surveyor's rod or wading rod
2. Pick up the particle at the toe of your boot (or wading rod tip)
   and measure its intermediate axis (b-axis) to the nearest mm
   using the metric ruler. Record the measurement on the field form.
3. If the particle cannot be picked up (bedrock, hardpan), record
   the appropriate size class code.
4. Record the presence or absence of **coarse particulate organic
   matter (CPOM)** at each point. CPOM includes leaves, needles,
   twigs, bark, and other organic material greater than 1 mm but no
   larger than 10 cm.

Substrate size classes for reference:

| Code | Class         | Size Range (mm)     |
|:-----|:--------------|:--------------------|
| RS   | Bedrock       | Smooth, continuous   |
| RR   | Bedrock       | Rough, irregular     |
| HP   | Hardpan       | Hardite /ite soil  |
| BL   | Boulder       | > 250                |
| CB   | Cobble        | 64--250              |
| GC   | Coarse gravel | 16--64               |
| GF   | Fine gravel   | 2--16                |
| SA   | Sand          | 0.06--2              |
| FN   | Fines         | < 0.06 (silt/clay)  |
| WD   | Wood          | --                   |
| OT   | Other         | Concrete, metal, etc.|

This produces 105 substrate measurements per reach (5 points at 21
transects), providing robust characterization of the streambed.

### 7.5 Module E: Cobble Embeddedness

At each of the five substrate measurement points (main transects
only), if the particle is gravel, cobble, or boulder:

1. Estimate the percentage of the particle surface that is
   surrounded (embedded) by fine sediment (sand, silt, clay)
2. Record to the nearest 5% or 10%
3. Sand and finer substrates are defined as 100% embedded by
   convention
4. Bedrock is not assessed for embeddedness

### 7.6 Module F: Algal and Macrophyte Cover

At each of the five substrate measurement points (main and
inter-transects):

1. Record presence or absence of **macroalgae** (filamentous green
   algae, *Cladophora*, etc.) on the substrate particle
2. Record presence or absence of **macrophytes** (rooted vascular
   aquatic plants). Mosses are explicitly excluded from macrophytes.
3. At main transects, estimate and record percent cover of
   macroalgae and macrophytes within a 1 m radius of the point

### 7.7 Module G: Bank Stability

At each main transect, assess bank stability for both left and right
banks along the imaginary line from the wetted margin to the bankfull
boundary:

1. Estimate the **percent of the bank covered by erosion** (exposed
   bare soil, slumping, undercutting). Record to the nearest 5%.
2. Estimate the **angle of the bank** (undercut, vertical, steep,
   gradual, flat)

### 7.8 Module H: Human Influence

At each main transect, looking 5 m upstream and 5 m downstream from
the transect and extending 10 m shoreward from each bank, record the
proximity of the following human influences for both left and right
banks:

| Category                      | Record as           |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------|
| Walls, rip-rap, dams          | 0 = absent, P = present > 10 m, C = present within 10 m, B = present on bank |
| Buildings                     | 0, P, C, or B       |
| Pavement or cleared lot       | 0, P, C, or B       |
| Road or railroad              | 0, P, C, or B       |
| Pipes (inlet/outlet)          | 0, P, C, or B       |
| Landfill or trash             | 0, P, C, or B       |
| Park or lawn                  | 0, P, C, or B       |
| Row crops                     | 0, P, C, or B       |
| Pasture, range, or hay field  | 0, P, C, or B       |
| Logging operations            | 0, P, C, or B       |
| Mining activity               | 0, P, C, or B       |

### 7.9 Module I: Riparian Vegetation

At each main transect, looking 5 m upstream and 5 m downstream from
the transect and extending 10 m shoreward from each bank, estimate
the areal cover of riparian vegetation in three layers for both left
and right banks:

| Layer              | Description                                    |
|:-------------------|:-----------------------------------------------|
| Canopy (> 5 m)     | Trees and tall shrubs forming the upper canopy |
| Understory (0.5--5 m) | Shrubs, saplings, and tall herbaceous plants |
| Ground cover (< 0.5 m) | Grasses, forbs, mosses, leaf litter          |

For each layer, estimate cover as: 0 = absent, 1 = sparse
(< 10%), 2 = moderate (10--40%), 3 = heavy (40--75%),
4 = very heavy (> 75%). Also record the dominant vegetation type
(deciduous, coniferous, mixed, herbaceous, or absent).

### 7.10 Module J: Instream Habitat Complexity

At each main transect, estimate the areal cover of the following
instream habitat features within the wetted channel, looking 5 m
upstream and 5 m downstream:

| Feature                       | Record cover class (0--4) |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------------|
| Large woody debris (> 10 cm diameter, > 1 m length) | 0--4 |
| Overhanging vegetation        | 0--4                      |
| Undercut banks                | 0--4                      |
| Boulders (> 25 cm)            | 0--4                      |
| Submergent macrophytes        | 0--4                      |
| Emergent macrophytes          | 0--4                      |
| Other (specify)               | 0--4                      |

Cover classes: 0 = absent, 1 = sparse (< 10%), 2 = moderate
(10--40%), 3 = heavy (40--75%), 4 = very heavy (> 75%).

Estimates should include only features within the wetted margin of
the stream.

### 7.11 Module K: Stream Shading (Densiometer Readings)

At each main transect, measure canopy cover with the convex spherical
densiometer:

1. Stand at the center of the stream facing each of the four cardinal
   directions (upstream, downstream, left bank, right bank)
2. Hold the densiometer level at elbow height and count the number
   of grid intersections covered by reflected canopy
3. Record each of the four readings on the field form
4. For streams wider than 10 m, also take one reading at each bank
   (left and right), for a total of six readings per transect

### 7.12 Module L: Slope and Sinuosity

**Slope (clinometer method):**

1. Two crew members stand at adjacent main transects (e.g., A and B)
2. Each person holds the clinometer (or autolevel stadia rod) at the
   same height above the water surface
3. Sight to the other person's eye level and record the angle
4. Repeat for all adjacent transect pairs from A to K
5. Calculate overall reach slope from the cumulative elevation change
   divided by the reach length

**Sinuosity:**

1. At each main transect, record a compass bearing looking upstream
   to the next transect
2. Calculate sinuosity as: reach length divided by the straight-line
   distance from Transect A to Transect K (measured from GPS
   coordinates)

### 7.13 Module M: Photographs

At a minimum, take the following photographs:

1. Upstream view from Transect A
2. Downstream view from Transect K
3. Representative view at each main transect (upstream or
   cross-channel)
4. Close-up of any unusual features (engineered structures, large
   woody debris jams, erosion, invasive species, pollution sources)

Use a consistent naming convention:
`YYYY-MM-DD_SiteID_TransectID_Direction.jpg`

### 7.14 Module N: Flow Habitat Types (Inter-Transect)

Between each pair of main transects, visually classify the dominant
flow habitat type:

| Code | Habitat Type  | Description                                |
|:-----|:--------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| GL   | Glide         | Slow, smooth, laminar flow; moderate depth |
| PO   | Pool          | Deep, negligible current                   |
| RI   | Riffle        | Shallow, fast, turbulent, broken surface   |
| RU   | Run           | Moderate depth, moderate current, unbroken surface |
| CA   | Cascade       | Steep, fast flow over boulders/bedrock     |
| RA   | Rapids        | Fast, deep, turbulent                      |
| FA   | Falls         | Vertical or near-vertical drop             |
| DR   | Dry           | No surface water                           |

Record the dominant flow habitat type and estimate its percentage of
the inter-transect distance.

### 7.15 Module O: Stream Discharge (Optional)

If discharge is measured concurrently, follow
[SOP-F42 Stream Discharge Measurement](SOP-F42-stream-discharge-measurement.qmd).
Select a cross-section near the downstream end of the reach (at or
near Transect A) that meets discharge measurement criteria. If a
current meter is not available, the neutrally buoyant object (NBO)
method may be used as a rough estimate (see SWAMP SOP Section 8.1.2).

### 7.16 Module P: Post-Sampling Qualitative Observations

After completing all transect measurements, walk the full reach and
record qualitative observations on the field form:

- Channel constraint (confined, moderately confined, unconfined)
- Dominant channel type (riffle-pool, step-pool, plane-bed, dune-
  ripple, cascade, braided)
- Evidence of channelization or channel modification
- Dominant riparian land use (natural, agriculture, urban/suburban,
  mixed)
- Aquatic and riparian invasive species observed (e.g., *Arundo
  donax*, *Tamarix* spp., New Zealand mudsnails)
- Wildlife observations relevant to site characterization


## 8. Data Management

### 8.1 Field Data Entry

- Complete all field data sheets before leaving the site
- Have a second crew member review the sheets for completeness and
  legibility
- Scan or photograph field sheets at the end of each field day as a
  backup

### 8.2 Electronic Data Entry

1. Enter data into the project database or spreadsheet within 48
   hours of collection
2. Use the SWAMP-compatible data format if data will be submitted to
   the California Environmental Data Exchange Network (CEDEN)
3. All data entry scripts should be version-controlled per
   [SOP-L07 RStudio and GitHub](../lab_sops/SOP-L07-rstudio-github.qmd)

### 8.3 Calculating the Index of Physical-habitat Integrity (IPI)

The IPI is a multimetric index that integrates physical habitat
metrics into a single score of habitat condition. IPI scores range
from 0 (highly degraded) to 1 (reference condition). Calculation
requires the full set of SWAMP physical habitat modules (C through
M) and is performed in R using the SWAMP bioassessment tools. See
@rehn2017 for methodology and interpretation guidance.


## 9. Quality Control

### 9.1 Measurement Quality Objectives

| Measurement             | Precision Target                         |
|:------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Wetted width            | Replicate measurements within 5%         |
| Substrate particle size | Replicate measurements within one size class |
| Depth                   | Replicate measurements within 2 cm       |
| Densiometer readings    | Replicate within 5 grid intersections    |
| Embeddedness            | Replicate within 10%                     |

### 9.2 Duplicate Sampling

For SWAMP-comparable data, duplicate physical habitat assessments
are required at 10% of study sites. A second crew independently
measures the same reach within the same day or (ideally) within 48
hours.

### 9.3 Common Errors to Avoid

- Measuring transects out of sequence (always work upstream)
- Inconsistent bankfull identification between crew members
  (calibrate as a group at the first transect)
- Forgetting to record GPS coordinates at Transects A and K
- Omitting inter-transect measurements (they are required for full
  IPI calculation)
- Failing to record the measurement units (mm vs. size class code)
  for substrate

## 11. Training Record

Before conducting physical habitat assessments independently,
personnel must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-F01 Field Safety](SOP-F01-field-safety.qmd),
   and the SWAMP Supplemental Guidance Document in full
2. Review the SWAMP physical habitat field data sheets and understand
   all fields
3. Participate in a calibration exercise for bankfull identification
   and substrate measurement with an experienced crew leader
4. Complete at least one full reach assessment under the supervision
   of a trained operator, with substrate and embeddedness estimates
   that agree with the trainer within the precision targets in
   Section 9.1
5. Demonstrate proper densiometer technique and slope measurement
6. Be signed off by the PI or field lead


## Appendix A: Field Data Sheets {.appendix}

SWAMP Bioassessment Field Data Sheets (including physical habitat
forms) are available by request from
[SWAMP\@waterboards.ca.gov](mailto:SWAMP@waterboards.ca.gov) or can
be downloaded from:
<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/water_issues/programs/swamp/bioassessment/sops.html>

Print on waterproof paper (e.g., Rite in the Rain) for field use.

The following forms are needed for a complete physical habitat
assessment:

1. Station Information and Notable Field Conditions
2. Channel/Riparian Cross-Section and Thalweg Profile (one per
   transect)
3. Slope and Bearing
4. Post-Sampling Qualitative Observations
5. Discharge Measurement (if applicable)


## Appendix B: Quick Reference -- Transect Layout {.appendix}

For a 150 m reach (average wetted width 10 m or less):

| Transect | Station (m) | Type          |
|:---------|:------------|:--------------|
| A        | 0           | Main          |
| AB       | 7.5         | Inter         |
| B        | 15          | Main          |
| BC       | 22.5        | Inter         |
| C        | 30          | Main          |
| CD       | 37.5        | Inter         |
| D        | 45          | Main          |
| DE       | 52.5        | Inter         |
| E        | 60          | Main          |
| EF       | 67.5        | Inter         |
| F        | 75          | Main          |
| FG       | 82.5        | Inter         |
| G        | 90          | Main          |
| GH       | 97.5        | Inter         |
| H        | 105         | Main          |
| HI       | 112.5       | Inter         |
| I        | 120         | Main          |
| IJ       | 127.5       | Inter         |
| J        | 135         | Main          |
| JK       | 142.5       | Inter         |
| K        | 150         | Main          |

For a 250 m reach (average wetted width greater than 10 m), multiply
all station distances by 250/150 (transects are 25 m apart;
inter-transects at 12.5 m intervals).


## Appendix C: Substrate Size Class Quick Reference {.appendix}

| Code | Class          | Size Range (mm)         | Field ID                      |
|:-----|:---------------|:------------------------|:------------------------------|
| RS   | Bedrock smooth | Continuous              | Cannot be moved               |
| RR   | Bedrock rough  | Continuous              | Cannot be moved; irregular surface |
| HP   | Hardpan        | Continuous              | Compacted clay/ite layer     |
| BL   | Boulder        | > 250                   | Cannot be lifted with one hand |
| CB   | Cobble         | 64--250                 | Tennis ball to basketball     |
| GC   | Coarse gravel  | 16--64                  | Marble to tennis ball         |
| GF   | Fine gravel    | 2--16                   | Ladybug to marble             |
| SA   | Sand           | 0.06--2                 | Gritty; individual grains visible |
| FN   | Fines          | < 0.06                  | Smooth; no individual grains felt |
| WD   | Wood           | --                      | Any size                      |
| OT   | Other          | --                      | Concrete, metal, trash, etc.  |

Always measure the intermediate axis (b-axis) of the particle.
